title: Ghana appoint Carlos Quieroz as head coach for 2026 World Cup
content:
Carlos Quieroz has been appointed as Ghana head coach ahead of the 2026 World Cup.

The 73-year-old has coached Iran at each of the last three World Cup finals, having taken Portugal to the last-16 stage of the 2010 edition.

Quieroz, whose coaching career has spanned 36 years, replaces Otto Addo, who was sacked earlier this month.

Ghana have lost each of their last four matches including friendly losses to Austria (5-1) and Germany (2-1), having missed out on qualification for this winter’s Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON).

Quieroz’s first game in charge will be a friendly against Mexico at a yet-to-be-announced venue in Mexico on May 22 before a final pre-tournament warm-up match against Wales at the Cardiff City Stadium on June 2.

Ghana’s will play their World Cup Group L opener against Panama in Toronto on June 17.

Ghana face England in their second World Cup group match, in Massachusetts on June 23 before concluding their group-stage campaign against Croatia in Philadelphia on June 27.

Analysis by Carl Anka

For Premier League viewers, Queiroz’s reputation is linked to his years working as one of Ferguson’s assistants at Manchester United, helping the team adapt to a fluid attacking 4-3-3 that would eventually conquer Europe in 2008 with a Champions League title.

His record at international level makes for a stark contrast. Queiroz is one of the more well-journeyed and defensively pragmatic coaches in the world. He spent eight years in charge of Iran between 2011-19 before a disastrous and brief spell in charge of Colombia.

He took charge of Egypt and nearly won the 2021 AFCON with the side putting in a series of defensively resolute performances that were low in entertainment. The Egyptian team, centred around Mohammed Salah, would end up losing to Senegal in the final in a penalty shootout.

Queiroz returned to Iran for a second stint in September 2022 leading the team in the World Cup, which included a 6-2 defeat to England in the group stage.
